# Introduction

This study examines whether book cover color is associated with the book genre.

# Literature Review

Others have previously studied how machine learning algorithims may predict information about a book including a book's genre [@vayadande2024book].


# Method(A)
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency


domain = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/"
path = "adamrossnelson/confident/refs/heads/main/data/"
file = "confident_fictional_books.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(domain + path + file)
```
Our null hypothesis is that book cover color does not predict the book's genre
while the alternate hypothesis is that book cober color does predict the book's
genre and we study this question with data from `{python}` f"{books.shape[0]}"`
books where we know the book's genre and the book 's cover color such that we 
can conduct a chi2 test to see if these two variables
are either independent or dependent (as it turns out our chi2 test will involve
a 
`{python} f"{df['book_genre'].nunique()}"` x
`{python} f"{df['book_color'].nunique()}"` test).


# Results
```{python}
# Conduct the chi2 with chi2_contingency by passing the observed
x2, pval, degf, _ = chi2_contingency(
    pd.crosstab(
       df['book_genre'],
       df['book_color']))
```

Results: Chi2 Stat: `{python} f"{x2:.5f}"` - Pvalue: `{python} f"{pval:.5f}"` - 
Degree of Freedom: `{python} f"{degf}"`.


With a Chi2 Stat: `{python} f"{x2:.5f}"` and a p-value nearly equal to `{python} f"{pval:.5f}"` (degrees
of freedom `{python} f"{degf}"`) we fail to reject our null
hypothesis and conclude that given these data, and given
this analytical approach, there is no evidence to believe
that a book's cover color may predict that book's genre.
